comparison: Both evaluate the mitfaCas9 line generation (C1-C9). OpenEval finds all evidence SUPPORTED with converging validation. Peer reviewers find the approach UNCERTAIN, accepting it as 'convincing' overall but specifically questioning the quantification of 86% Cas9 expression (C9) shown in Figure 1C.

Both evaluate albino knockout experiments (C12-C19). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED emphasizing progressive phenotype and CRISPR-seq validation. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, describing it as successful 'demonstration of method's efficiency' with clean figures and appropriate controls. Strong agreement.

Both evaluate sox10 experiments (C23-C31). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, highlighting quantified phenotypes and regeneration insights. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, praising demonstration of non-cell autonomous mechanisms and ability to bypass embryonic lethality. Strong agreement, though peer review focuses on C23-C31 while OpenEval also includes C20-C22.

Both evaluate tuba1a experiments (C33-C46). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED while acknowledging mechanism remains 'somewhat speculative' (C40). Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, finding results 'striking' but cautioning that 'mechanistic explanations are minimally interrogated' and should be treated as 'inspiration rather than bona fide truth.' Disagreement on confidence level.

Both evaluate melanoma modeling (C50-C61). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, emphasizing dose-dependent tumor incidence and molecular validation. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, describing data as 'convincing' and noting the system facilitates multiplexed sgRNA approaches. Strong agreement, though peer review excludes C47-C49.

Both evaluate sox10 knockout in melanoma (C64-C67, C85-C86). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN due to small sample size (2/3 tumors for sox9 upregulation) and qualitative invasion assessment. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED, calling it 'a beautiful demonstration' of SOX10/SOX9 reciprocal regulation. Significant disagreement on data sufficiency.

OpenEval R6 includes human cell line re-analysis (C69) as part of broader UNCERTAIN evaluation of sox10/sox9 findings. Peer R7 separately evaluates C69 as SUPPORTED cross-species validation. Peer reviewers view this analysis more favorably when considered independently.

OpenEval R6 includes C87 (in vivo vs in vitro differences) in broader UNCERTAIN evaluation. Peer R9 separately rates C87 as SUPPORTED, explicitly endorsing that unexpected in vivo phenotypes emerge that aren't predicted from in vitro studies. Peer reviewers view this conclusion more positively.

Both evaluate summary claims about technological achievement (C82-C84). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, noting claims are well-supported by experimental results but advantage of endogenous regulatory elements (C90) not directly tested. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, concluding the system is 'convincing' and a 'welcome addition.' Strong agreement.

Both address C90 regarding endogenous regulatory elements. OpenEval notes in R7 that this advantage is 'stated but not directly tested through comparison with promoter-fragment approaches.' Peer R10 rates UNCERTAIN, noting 'no direct comparison is made with other tools' like MAZERATI and experimentation would be appreciated. Agreement that claim lacks direct experimental support.

OpenEval R8 evaluates cited prior work and established biological knowledge (C5-C6, C70-C79, C88-C89, C91-C93) as SUPPORTED with appropriate references. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background/citation claims.

Peer R10 evaluates C89 and C90 together regarding comparison with other tools. OpenEval addresses C90 in R7 and C89 in R8 (as cited work), but does not have a dedicated evaluation matching peer R10's focus on comparative tool assessment.
